request: Add helpers in hc/front/views.py to load a check by code for the current user and block read-only members from writing.

summary.result_text:
I added `_get_check_for_user` and `_get_rw_check_for_user` to `hc/front/views.py`, just above `_get_channel_for_user`. `python -m py_compile` passes, but I haven't run the test suite.

- **`_get_check_for_user(request, code, preload_owner_profile=False)`** returns `(check, rw)`. Superusers and the project owner get `rw=True`. Other users must be a project `Member`, otherwise they get a 404, and `rw` comes from `membership.is_rw`. It follows the same pattern as `_get_channel_for_user`. With `preload_owner_profile=True` it also fetches `project__owner__profile` in the same query.
- **`_get_rw_check_for_user(request, code)`** calls the first helper and raises `PermissionDenied` if the user is read-only. Otherwise it returns just the check.

The file already called both helpers in 16 places, for example `check, rw = _get_check_for_user(request, code, preload_owner_profile=True)`, but neither was defined anywhere. The new helpers match those call signatures, so I didn't touch any callers.

`Profile` has a one-to-one link to `User`, so the `project__owner__profile` lookup should resolve.

input.old_string: def _get_channel_for_user(request: HttpRequest, code: UUID) -> tuple[Channel, bool]:

input.command: python -m py_compile hc/front/views.py && echo ok; grep -n "owner.*profile\|related_name" hc/accounts/models.py | head
grep -n "class Profile" -A8 hc/accounts/models.py | grep -n "user"; sed -n 462,472p hc/accounts/models.py
